items.item: The Chinese term for how far a claim has been seen (08 §2, now 'How far it has been seen: labels and bases')
items.how: Label, column head and glossary name: 看到了多远, as ONE-PAGE.zh, THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.zh, README-ZH and OPENING.zh already write it in headings and column heads; 了 carries the English 'has been'. In prose it stays a clause (诸结果各看到了多远, 先说各自看到了多远), which plain Chinese needs no noun for. Where a noun is unavoidable: 看到的程度 (used once, in lineage.json's translation of 'where vocabulary, method, structure or standing changed'). Why: the same verb as the label, so a reader meets one term; 程度 is a neutral degree and carries no rank, status or hierarchy, unlike 地位 (social status, the thing the meta-attractor concerns), 等级 or 身份; 所见程度 is literary and not an established collocation, and 所见 alone reads as 'what is seen'. 08 §7's other sense, a central declaration's standing against the edge of one root (derived, under a stated hypothesis, counting, at a named distance), is rendered 位置, as the zh fronts already do since pass 3: it is a place against the root's edge, not how far a claim has been seen, and 08 §7 keeps 'standing against the edge' in its sentence (its lead is now 'How far the root reaches').

items.item: GLOSSARY.zh.md: the term's row, renamed, its old anchor kept
items.how: The row 地位（standing） is now 看到了多远（how far seen）, mirroring GLOSSARY.md as the terms agent rewrote it ('what kind of claim a statement is and how far it has been seen, as its label says'). Anchors <a id="standing"> (the English row's new id), <a id="看到了多远"> and <a id="地位"> (the old name; no link used it, since the row had no explicit anchor). One line says that before 9 November 2026 the English called it standing and the Chinese edition 地位, which in Chinese mostly means social status; one line says how to write it (看到了多远 as a head or name, a clause in prose, 看到的程度 where a noun is needed) and that a central declaration's place against the root's edge is another thing (see 根之边). The 论题 row says 附上它看到了多远 … （T8 已论证，未经检验）, as the English row now does. 根之边, 推导而得 and 指明的距离 now say 位置 (根之边 also names the four places, 08 §7's own list).
